payload.name: Count owned pets via acquisition events
payload.description: When a question asks how many of a pet/animal type a person has or owns, use acquisition/ownership event searches before concluding no information.
content: When the question is a count of owned items (e.g., 'how many dogs does Andrew have?'), run an acquisition-focused search using the person's name plus ownership terms such as 'adopted', 'adoption', 'owns', 'got', and pet-type synonyms (dog/puppy/pup, cat/kitten).
Aggregate distinct named individuals from current (active) event memories about that person; exclude plans, considerations, other people's pets, and repeated mentions of the same pet.
Stop after one focused acquisition search if all owned items are identified or it returns no new candidates; do not exhaustively expand.

solves: The failure mechanism is that count-of-owned-things questions are answered after a single generic keyword query that misses the adoption/ownership event memories naming each item, so the agent falsely reports no information. This Skill applies when a future question asks 'how many X does Y have/own' where X is a pet or possession, and the needed evidence is distributed across acquisition events. It must not apply to questions about a single known entity, someone else's pets, or plans/considerations that do not establish current ownership.
